pr_metadata.title: feat(release): resume from the first undone stage
pr_metadata.summary: Each tracked vrg-release stage now records itself done, with the PRs, tag and CD runs later stages need, in the tracking issue's state block, and --resume reads that block under the identity rule, verifies its facts against GitHub and git, and runs only the stages not yet done (Task 4 of epic vergil-project/.github#1440).
pr_metadata.notes:
Merge review: done: eligible; accepted-risk 0

- Resume preflight runs only the host, auth and config checks; it adopts the release worktree only when the first undone stage is at or before teardown-worktree, which is now fail-fast. find_resume_target now requires a state block and refuses an issue without one (old tooling), with no fallback to the checklist.
- verify_facts checks the merged PRs, the main and develop CD runs' head SHAs, and that the tag peels to tag_commit, which is the release merge commit or a single-parent commit on top of it. confirm-main now records tag_commit.
- Review point: a stage that returns without doing its work is not recorded done, so a resume runs it again: promote skipped by --no-promote or a deferred package-index, a close-finalize that left the issue open, and a consumer-refresh that ran no command (held, not run after a failed stage, or --no-install).
- Review point: a failure after close-finalize has closed the tracking issue (update-deps or consumer-refresh) cannot be resumed, since --resume finds only open issues. This comes from the current stage order; Tasks 8 and 10 reorder the stages so close-tracking comes last.
- The deferral comment, publish-status and finalize no longer say not to resume: they now say to re-run the publish, then finish with vrg-release --resume, which also does the promote a deferred index held back.
- Removed the now-unused checklist cursor (tracking.cursor, checklist.has_block, checklist.first_unchecked).
- Docs: new Resuming a release section in the releasing guide; release reference updated.
